transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to discuss the discharge plan for our patient who's leaving tomorrow with a seven-day outpatient antibiotic course. As we all know, the current formulary option is daily IV ceftriaxone, but the patient would prefer an oral option if we can arrange something clinically and operationally appropriate. Linezolid is available as a restricted nonformulary oral option. Before I finalize any authorization, I need to follow our routine practice and check with infectious disease, utilization review, and specialty-pharmacy coordination. Could I get input from each of those areas so we can determine the best path forward?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: The finalized culture report shows the organism is susceptible to linezolid but resistant to the available oral alternatives, and my treatment plan calls for linezolid 600 mg twice daily for exactly six days after discharge.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: From a utilization review standpoint, I need to flag an important coverage issue. The patient's insurer will authorize the restricted linezolid only if the prior-authorization submission includes the culture result, the exact 600 mg twice-daily regimen, and a six-day duration. A submission for the formulary IV ceftriaxone option does not satisfy the patient's outpatient coverage pathway. So if we're going with linezolid, the PA needs all three of those elements included.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From specialty-pharmacy coordination: The specialty pharmacy has confirmed that linezolid can be delivered to the patient's home tomorrow between 8:00 and 9:00 AM. Importantly, the patient has no transportation available to collect it, so that delivery window must be recorded in the discharge plan.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Submit PA with culture results, 600 mg twice-daily regimen, and six-day duration as required for linezolid coverage authorization.
Confirm home delivery between 8:00 and 9:00 AM tomorrow and record the delivery window in the discharge plan.
Finalize discharge with oral linezolid regimen, ensuring patient education on 600 mg twice-daily dosing for six days.
